chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

You wipe with your right hand upon your forehead and your face at the end of Al-Maghrib prayer and the other prayers, and you say: 'In the Name of Allah, the Knower of the Hidden and the Apparent, the Beneficent, the Merciful, Who there is no god except Him. O Allah! I seek Refuge with You from worry, grief, sickness, deficiency, lowliness, disgrace, and immoralities, whatever is apparent of them and whatever is hidden.'

key_terms.عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَ الشَّهَادَةِ: The Knower of the Hidden and the Apparent

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and action after Maghrib prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes the specific act of masah (wiping) on the forehead and face with the right hand after Maghrib and other prayers, a practice central to Shia ritual jurisprudence. The accompanying supplication invokes Allah’s attributes as the Knower of the unseen and seen, seeking refuge from both manifest and hidden afflictions, thereby linking physical ritual with spiritual protection.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Abu Ismail Al Sarraj, from Ali Bin Shajara, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Wipe your right hand upon your forehead and your face at the end of Al-Maghrib (Salāt), and (other) Salāts, and you should be saying, ‘In the Name of Allahazwj Who, there is no god except for Himazwj, the Knower of the hidden and the apparent, the Beneficent, the Merciful! O Allahazwj! I seek Refuge with Youazwj from the worries, and the grief, and the sickness, and the deficiencies, and lowliness, and the disgrace, and the immoralities, whatever is apparent from these and what is hidden’.
en.sarwar: 24. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from abu ’Isma‘il al-Sarraj from Ali ibn Shajarah from Muhammad ibn Marwan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Wipe with your right hand your forehead after Maghrib Salah (prayer) after sunset and other Salawat (prayers) and say, “In the name of Allah besides whom no one deserves to be worshipped. He has the knowledge of the unseen and seen, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O Lord, I seek refuge with You against anxiety, sadness, illness, deficiencies, lowliness, humiliation and the apparent and concealed indecencies.’””
